subject: Post-call recap: Decision roles, procurement timeline, and redline sequencing
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@cedarlane.com>, Marcus Li <marcus.li@cedarlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Decision roles, procurement timeline, and redline sequencing

Hi Dana / Marcus —

Great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key takeaways
- Economic buyer: Marcus Li (VP Product) — will own budget approval and final sign-off.
- Security & procurement: Olivia Chen (Head of InfoSec) will run the DPA/security questionnaire; procurement will handle commercial terms and MSA routing.
- Primary use case: personalized product recommendations (low-PHI, but high traffic).

Action items (owner / ETA)
1) CedarLane: share stakeholder contact for procurement (Dana) — by Thu 6/17
2) Redwood: send NDA and a light MSA redline guidance doc (Hannah / Ben) — EOD 6/15 (attached)
3) Redwood Security: send our standard DPA and SOC summary; offer 1:1 with security (Aditya) — suggest availability next week
4) Plan: We recommend a two-week pilot (staging -> 4-week evaluation) after NDA; propose kickoff early July.

Questions for you:
- Typical procurement turn time once procurement has the MSA and SOW? (helps set expectations)
- Who on your side should legal loop in for redlines (name & email)?

I'll attach the stakeholder matrix template and the NDA. Ben — can you add the cost estimate + pilot SOW and drop into the shared Drive link?

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Decision roles, procurement timeline, and redline sequencing

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications and our timelines: 

Stakeholders from CedarLane
- Economic buyer: Marcus Li (VP Product) — final sign-off, buying authority up to $250k.
- Procurement lead: Dana Ortiz (me) — will coordinate PO and vendor setup.
- Legal contact for MSA redlines: Olivia Chen (legal counsel) — olivia.chen@cedarlane.com
- InfoSec: Kevin Park (contractor) will run the questionnaire — kevin.park@cedarlane.com (cc'd below)

Procurement cadence
- NDA: 1–2 business days turnaround once we get a standard PDF (we can sign via DocuSign).
- MSA: typical redline cycle is 7–12 business days depending on complexity; procurement wants to see commercial terms (price, SOW, termination).
- DPA/Security review: this runs parallel but may extend depending on SOC evidence; Kevin will flag any gating issues early.

I'll share the internal stakeholder contact list by EOD. For the MSA, please send an annotated guidance doc so legal knows which clauses you consider non-negotiable.

—Dana
Dana Ortiz
Head of Procurement | CedarLane Systems
dana.ortiz@cedarlane.com

Hi Dana / Marcus —

Thanks — attaching a short "what matters" guidance doc for legal review (MSA_redline_guidance.docx) and an initial pilot SOW + ballpark pricing. Highlights:
- Pilot: 2-week staging integration + 4-week evaluation, capped tokens and SLA commitments for production tests.
- Pricing: pilot discount applied; committed pricing options for Dedicated if pilot passes.
- Non-negotiable asks we expect: retention limits for raw logs, standard indemnity language, and a 30-day termination for convenience.

Soojin (cc) can take point on the legal redline guidance if Olivia wants a quick sync. Aditya — let's lock security 1:1 options for next Wed/Thu.

Next step: Dana — once you send Olivia's contact, Soojin will propose a prioritized clause list and a recommended redline path (fast-track vs full review).

Cheers,
Ben

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Decision roles, procurement timeline, and redline sequencing

Thanks all. Quick read-through notes from Legal: 

1) NDA: standard — we can sign but please confirm Redwood's retention window for emailed attachments.
2) MSA: main items we'll touch: liability cap, data handling (esp. production telemetry), and termination clauses. I prefer an initial fast-path redline:
   - Round 1: commercial (pricing/SOW) + a 1-page legal summary (3 business days)
   - Round 2: detailed legal redlines (7 business days)

3) DPA/Security: Kevin will run the questionnaire; SOC artifacts can be submitted to our secure portal.

If Redwood can provide a 1-pager that maps clauses to our requests (Ben's guidance doc looks useful), we can often compress to a 7–10 business-day total window. Otherwise plan for 2+ weeks.

Olivia Chen
Legal Counsel | CedarLane Systems
olivia.chen@cedarlane.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Decision roles, procurement timeline, and redline sequencing

Olivia / Dana — thanks for the clarity. Proposal from Redwood legal to keep things tight: 

Suggested sequencing (Redwood recommended)
- Day 0: NDA executed (DocuSign) — clears data sharing for security review.
- Day 1–3: Commercial + 1-page clause map submitted by Redwood (Ben / Soojin).
- Day 3–6: Procurement/Legal quick-pass (Olivia) — accept core commercial points or flag 1–3 gating clauses.
- Day 6–12: Full legal redline to close (if needed).

Turn-time commitments
- Redwood: 48–72 hour turnaround for each redline iteration during the quick-pass.
- CedarLane: recommended to assign one legal approver for the pilot SOW to keep cycles short.

Next steps (owners)
- Ben: finalize a 1-page clause map + updated SOW (EOD Thu 6/17).
- Hannah: send DocuSign NDA for signature (today).
- Aditya: share security availability for a 30-minute call (options Wed/Thu next week).

If that sequencing works we can tentatively target pilot kickoff week of July 6th.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
